page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.48xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture. Powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9T24 processors running at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz, this instance delivers a total of 192 dedicated vCPUs. The architecture utilizes KVM virtualization, providing isolation for high-concurrency computing tasks.

The instance is provisioned with 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding a compute-dense ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It features no local disk storage, relying entirely on remote block storage solutions for persistent data needs. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline network bandwidth of 64 Gbps, facilitating rapid data transfers across cluster nodes and distributed cloud resources.

Optimized for compute-intensive workloads that benefit from a high core count without requiring extreme memory capacity per core, the ecs.c8a.48xlarge offers significant resource density. The provision of 192 vCPUs alongside high baseline network throughput supports scale-out parallel processing, electronic design automation, scientific simulations, batch processing pipelines, and high-performance web application backends.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.48xlarge is a high-density, compute-optimized instance powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9T24 processors running at 2.7 GHz. Utilizing KVM virtualization on x86_64 architecture, it delivers 192 dedicated vCPUs alongside 384.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of memory per core. The instance lacks local storage, depending on attached cloud block storage for persistent data, but compensates with a baseline network bandwidth of 64 Gbps to ensure high data throughput across distributed node clusters. Without GPU accelerators, the instance focuses on CPU-bound processing efficiency. The combination of dense vCPU count and high networking throughput makes the ecs.c8a.48xlarge suitable for heavily multithreaded compute workloads, continuous integration pipelines, batch data processing, scientific modeling, and enterprise backend microservices.
